s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of altered mental status and metabolic acidosis in a post-surgical patient
salient_findings: Severe metabolic acidosis with high anion gap
Normal renal function and absence of significant ketosis or lactic acidosis
key_facts: 75-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities
Recent prosthetic hip infection and revision surgery
Developed altered mental status on hospital day 10
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12
Vital signs: temperature 36.2°C, blood pressure 145/66 mmHg, pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Laboratory studies: sodium 142 mmol/L, potassium 3.5 mmol/L, chloride 118 mmol/L, bicarbonate 5 mmol/L
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L
Corrected anion gap of 25 mmol/L
Lactic acid 0.7 mmol/L, blood ketones <0.2 mmol/L, salicylate <0.4 mmol/L
Mildly elevated osmolar gap at 21 mOsm/kg

shortlist.label: Lactic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated anion gap and metabolic acidosis

shortlist.label: Sepsis-induced acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent prosthetic hip infection and revision surgery

shortlist.label: Uremic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic kidney disease and elevated creatinine

shortlist.label: Pyroglutamic acidemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated anion gap and metabolic acidosis, potential for acetaminophen-related toxicity

raw.rationale: The patient's high anion gap metabolic acidosis with a corrected anion gap of 25 mmol/L, low bicarbonate levels, and normal lactic acid levels are consistent with pyroglutamic acidemia, especially given the use of acetaminophen and the patient's renal impairment, which can increase the risk of this condition.

rejected.label: Lactic acidosis
rejected.why: The patient's lactic acid level is normal at 0.7 mmol/L, which does not support a diagnosis of lactic acidosis as the primary cause of the high anion gap metabolic acidosis.
